VO2max of a graded test, with maximality criteria

Source: R/VO2max_from_test.R
VO2max_from_test.Rd

Computes VO2max as the highest mean VO2 over `window` seconds of consecutive records (as `MFO()` does from `db_graded`) and checks whether the test was maximal, following the criteria reviewed by Howley, Bassett and Welch (1995, Med Sci Sports Exerc 27(9): 1292-1301, doi:10.1249/00005768-199509000-00009 ). The value is labelled `"VO2max"` when VO2 reached a plateau, or, without a plateau, when both the RER and the heart-rate criteria are met; otherwise it is labelled `"VO2peak"` (SPEC 14).

Usage

VO2max_from_test(
  db_graded,
  step_time,
  window = 30,
  age = NULL,
  HRmax_formula = c("tanaka", "fox"),
  plateau_threshold = 150,
  RER_threshold = 1.1,
  HR_threshold = 0.9
)

Arguments

db_graded

data frame of the graded test with `VO2` (ml/min) and, for the criteria, `RER`, `HR` (bpm) and `Load`.

step_time

how often the data were collected (s).

window

averaging window in seconds (default 30). If it is not a multiple of `step_time`, the number of records is rounded up and a message reports the effective window (as `vo2max_window` in [MFO()]).

age

age in years, for the predicted HRmax (optional).

HRmax_formula

`"tanaka"` (default) or `"fox"`.

plateau_threshold

VO2 increase between the last two stages below which there is a plateau, ml/min (default 150).

RER_threshold

RER above which the RER criterion is met (default 1.10).

HR_threshold

proportion of the predicted HRmax that the peak HR must reach (default 0.90).

Value

An object of class `MFO_VO2max`: a list with `VO2max` (ml/min), `type` (`"VO2max"` or `"VO2peak"`), `window` (effective, s), `window_requested`, `n_records`, `criteria` (a data frame with one row per criterion: `criterion`, `value`, `threshold`, `met`, `NA` when not evaluated), `HRmax_predicted`, `HRmax_formula` and `age`. It can be passed to [MFO()] as `VO2max`.

Details

Criteria (thresholds are arguments):

  • plateau: the mean VO2 of the last stage is less than `plateau_threshold` ml/min above that of the previous stage (150 ml/min, from Taylor et al. 1955 as reported by Howley et al. 1995). Stages are runs of equal `Load`, each averaged over its last `window` s; without a `Load` column the criterion is not evaluated.

  • RER: the highest `window`-s mean RER is above `RER_threshold`.

  • HR: the highest `window`-s mean HR is at least `HR_threshold` of the predicted HRmax. Needs `age`; without it the criterion is not evaluated and a warning says so.

Predicted HRmax: `"tanaka"` 208 - 0.7 x age (default; Tanaka, Monahan and Seals 2001, J Am Coll Cardiol 37(1): 153-156, doi:10.1016/s0735-1097(00)01054-8 ) or `"fox"` 220 - age, the equation in common use that Tanaka et al. (2001) revisit. The RER (1.10) and HR (90 %) thresholds are pending source verification (SPEC 19).

See also

[MFO()]

Examples

data(VO2max_df, package = "MFO")
VO2max_from_test(VO2max_df, step_time = 20, age = 30)
#> VO2max: a 30-s window is not a multiple of step_time (20 s); using 2 record(s) = 40 s.
#> <MFO_VO2max> VO2max = 3315.0 ml/min (highest 40-s mean)
#>   plateau  not met        value 247, threshold 150
#>   RER      met            value 1.16, threshold 1.1
#>   HR       met            value 0.987, threshold 0.9
